The Department of Geosciences brings together faculty, staff, students, alumni and community partners to explore Earth, the environment and society. Our programs in geography, environmental studies and geology are in-demand STEM fields that prepare students for meaningful careers. With a strong commitment to teaching, research and outreach, Auburn geoscientists contribute to the university’s land, sea and space grant missions while serving the people of Alabama and beyond.

Areas of Research
Earth and Life Through Time: sedimentology, paleobiology, geomicrobiology
Environmental Geosciences: climate, hydrogeology, environmental geochemistry, water resources, natural hazards
Geospatial Sciences and Geoinformatics: GIS, remote sensing, UAVs, data science
Natural Resources Exploration: energy, minerals, engineering geology
solid-earth: petrology, geochemistry, volcanology, structural geology, tectonics, geophysics
Geoscience Education and STEM Education: geocognition, climate and geoscience communication/STEM education
Human Geography: spatial patterns, human activity, cultural landscapes

Geo Explorer Auburn to represent Alabama in D.C. America250 parade
Geo Explorer Auburn, the world's largest mobile geosciences lab, is representing Alabama in the official National America250 Independence Day Parade in Washington, D.C. — and the most-celebrated mascot in America is tagging along.
Research and Innovation
Use an umbrella — rain or shine
Auburn climatologist Dr. Chandana Mitra explores how a simple umbrella can reduce heat exposure during Alabama's hottest months.
The faculty in Geosciences make a point to personally connect with students, which has encouraged me to explore different focus areas. The department is small and tight-knit, which has allowed me to form connections with peers and collaborate inside and outside the classroom.

Geology

The geoscience program at Auburn opened my eyes to areas of study that I didn't have a lot of experience with, like field work and economic geology. Being able to study these topics closely through opportunities in the department helped me realize I want to go into a career related to them!

Geology
Class of 2026
